issues.body:
This hunk deletes the `use proptest::prelude::*;`, `short_string()`, and the two `proptest!` metric-law tests — the only proptest consumers anywhere in sparq-nlq. I confirmed by grep over crates/sparq-nlq/{src,tests,examples,README.md}: after this PR the string "proptest" appears in exactly one place in the crate, crates/sparq-nlq/Cargo.toml:81, where it is still declared as a dev-dependency under the comment `# [GPT-5.6] sq-lxw27: metric-law coverage for deterministic dictionary ranking.`

Two consequences. (1) The dev-dependency is dead weight in sparq-nlq's dev graph — no build or CI impact (the repo has no cargo-machete/udeps gate, and proptest stays in Cargo.lock via sparq-core's own dev-dependency, so nothing goes red), but it is exactly the kind of leftover a consolidation PR should sweep. (2) More importantly, the comment is now a claim that does not trace to the code: the metric-law coverage it cites moved to crates/sparq-core/src/strdist.rs in this same PR. sparq-core's Cargo.toml is careful to document why proptest is dev-only; leaving a stale pointer in sparq-nlq undoes some of that care and will mislead the next reader into thinking sparq-nlq still owns metric-law tests.

Not a correctness, soundness, test-validity, or security issue — the four tests that remain in this file all pass and the ranking assertion at line 72 still exercises the real shared `edit_distance`.
issues.fix_hint: Drop the now-unused `proptest = "1"` dev-dependency and its `[GPT-5.6] sq-lxw27` comment from crates/sparq-nlq/Cargo.toml:79-81 (remove the whole `[dev-dependencies]` section if proptest is its only entry). If it is deliberately retained for imminent future proptests, retarget the comment so it no longer claims to justify metric-law coverage that now lives in crates/sparq-core/src/strdist.rs — e.g. point it at sq-lxw27's new home. Re-run `cargo test -p sparq-nlq` after the removal to confirm nothing else pulled it in.
issues.title: Removing the last proptest usage leaves sparq-nlq's `proptest` dev-dependency unused, with a now-false justifying comment

verdict.summary:
Round 3 adds exactly one thing over round 2: bench/feature-off-declarations/3822.json, the per-PR feature-OFF wasm declaration repairing the failing vectorized-feature-off leg. Verified against the mechanism: it matches the {pr, date, reason} shape in that directory's README and existing declarations (e.g. 1785.json); the gate is a set-difference on the directory listing, so a new <digits>.json satisfies it; and the reason's premise holds — crates/sparq-wasm/Cargo.toml:17 depends on sparq-core with default-features=false, so an always-compiled sparq-core addition can move feature-OFF bytes. The declaration governs INTENT only and defers size to the wasm_bundle_bytes ratchet, per the README's Scope section. The added code is purely additive and std-only, so it cannot leak a vectorized/default path — the declaration is not masking a real regression.

Re-verified the substance from round 2 against the checkout, not the diff text: cargo test -p sparq-core --lib strdist = 3 passed (basics + symmetry + triangle inequality); sparq-nlq --test constrain_unknown_terms = 4 passed; sparq-kb --features query --lib = 16 passed; RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check -p sparq-core -p sparq-nlq -p sparq-kb --all-targets --all-features clean; cargo build -p sparq-core --no-default-features clean (strdist is unconditional, pure std — sound in both feature states); RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p sparq-core --all-features clean (no feature-gated intra-doc-link trap); scripts/gate-api-skill.py G2 PASS; scripts/check-readme-template.py 0 deviations. The consolidated fn is byte-identical to both deleted copies, and the "é" assertion is non-vacuous (single-codepoint U+00E9, so a byte-oriented impl returns 2 and the test goes red).

One new hygiene leftover surfaced (below); the round-2 SKILL.md nit is unaddressed. Neither is blocker/major, so the verdict stays approve. Progress is "regressing" only by the literal scale — a new finding above round 2's sole nit.
